title: Forms: Validation and Accessibility
description: Learn how to create accessible forms with built-in HTML5 validation to improve user experience and data accuracy.

lessons.title: Introduction to Form Validation
lessons.content: Form validation ensures that users submit correct and complete information. HTML5 introduces built-in validation features that simplify this process.

lessons.title: Required Fields
lessons.content:
<input type="text" name="username" required>
<!-- This field must be filled before form submission -->

lessons.title: Using Pattern Attribute
lessons.content:
<input type="text" pattern="[A-Za-z]{3,}" title="Only letters, at least 3 characters">
<!-- Enforces a regex pattern on input -->

lessons.title: Min, Max, and Step Attributes
lessons.content:
<input type="number" min="1" max="10" step="1">
<!-- Restricts number inputs between 1 and 10 -->

lessons.title: The <label> Element
lessons.content: Labels improve accessibility by explicitly associating text with form controls, making forms easier to navigate for screen readers.

lessons.title: Using Fieldsets and Legends
lessons.content: Grouping related form controls with <fieldset> and describing them with <legend> enhances form structure and accessibility.

lessons.title: ARIA Roles and Attributes
lessons.content: Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA) roles help define accessible form elements and states for users relying on assistive technologies.

lessons.title: Custom Validation Messages
Accessibility Best Practices for Forms
lessons.content: Ensure all inputs have labels, use proper tab order, provide clear instructions, and make error messages descriptive.

lessons.title: Testing Form Accessibility and Validation
lessons.content: Use tools like browser dev tools, screen readers, and validation testing tools to ensure your forms are user-friendly and compliant.
